docs.flippable.component: `Flippable` is the card turn. It draws nothing — it ANSWERS one question: when the element is
turned over, which FACE shows? The answer is pure data, so a test reads it without a renderer
and a saved game reopens on the right side.
```ts
import { node, Bounded, Surfaced, Flippable, shownFace } from "game-kit"
const card = node("card",
Bounded({ bounds: rect(1, 1.4) }),
Surfaced({ surface: "queen" }),
Flippable({ reverse: "back", back: "tartan" }))
shownFace(card, true).surface   // "queen" — face-up is always the front
shownFace(card, false).surface  // "tartan" — the deck back
## The side is not stored here
Which side is up is RUNTIME state — the card is turned in the course of a game — so it is passed
to `shownFace`, never kept on the atom. `Flippable` describes how the down-side RELATES to the
up-side, which is spec: it does not change from turn to turn, so it belongs on the node and
crosses the wire once. That split is the same one `faceUp` teaches on every other stateful atom.
## The four reverses
The front is the node's `Surfaced.surface`. The reverse is one of four relations to it:
- `back` — a SEPARATE surface, usually a deck back shared by every card. The common case.
- `same` — the front again: a token that looks identical on both sides.
- `mirror` — the front, REFLECTED across the axis. The surface does not change; only a `mirror`
flag is raised, for a translucent tile seen from behind.
- `alt` — a separate surface too, but a per-card SECOND face rather than a shared back.
## A turn never blanks the card
`back`/`alt` name a reverse surface in `back`. Leave it empty and the turn falls back to the
front rather than showing nothing — a half-configured card stays playable. Requiring `Surfaced`
is the other half of that promise: no face, nothing to turn, and `shownFace` answers `undefined`.
## The axis
`axis` says which way the turn goes — `y` flips left-right, the usual card turn; `x` flips
top-over-bottom. It rides along in the answer even face-up, because the renderer needs it to
know which way a reflection would run.
## What this stand cannot show
`mirror` reflects the front, and the painter here has no axis-mirror, so on the glass `mirror`
reads as the front — which is exactly its surface. The reflection is a renderer capability, not
a fact of this atom; the atom's answer already carries the `mirror` flag for a painter that can.
docs.flippable.turn: One card and a switch that turns it. `faceUp` is the runtime side — the only thing `shownFace`
is told beyond the node itself. Flip it and the paint changes, because the resolver chose the
other surface: there is no second code path anywhere that says «the card is face-down».
The two colours are the front and the back. `reverse` is the relation between them — walk it
through its four values with the card face-down:
- `back` and `alt` swap the surface to the back colour.
- `same` keeps the front colour either way.
- `mirror` also keeps the front colour, and only means to reflect it — a reflection this stand
cannot paint, so it looks the same as face-up here. That is the surface it should show; the
turn it implies lives in the `mirror` flag the resolver returns, not on this glass.
Empty the back colour and turn the card: it does not go blank, it shows the front. That is the
same fallback the atom makes when a reverse surface is left unnamed.
